brief_text:
Trying to decide whether we bet the next two quarters on the AI copilot or finally do the platform rewrite. Or neither — I keep going back and forth, and I'm writing this partly to think. The goal I actually care about is 15% ARR growth next year without engineering attrition getting worse.

The copilot: the prototype demoed at SKO got the best reaction I've seen in years. Sales swears it would lift win rate from 22% to 30% — that number came from Marcus polling 15 AEs on Slack, so treat accordingly. Pricing thinks we could charge +£15/seat/month on our 40,000 seats, so up to £7.2m a year if attach were 100%, which it won't be — 25% attach feels honest, call it £1.8m. Build estimate is 4 engineers for 6 months. Actually, Elena's team said 6 engineers for 8 months once you include evals and the safety review — use hers, she's usually right. LLM serving cost is the thing nobody can pin down: finance modelled £3 per seat per month, could be half that or triple depending on caching. Assumption: our data-processing agreements let us send customer CRM text to a model provider — legal has NOT confirmed this, and if it's wrong the whole thing is dead in enterprise, which is 60% of revenue.

The rewrite: the platform is 9 years old, deploys take 45 minutes, and we lost two staff engineers to it last year — the exit interviews say so explicitly. Infra says the monolith adds roughly 30% drag to every feature — that's the number the CTO keeps quoting, source unclear, possibly the 2024 DX survey. Rewrite = 10 engineers, 12 months, and history says double whatever engineering estimates on this codebase. If we don't do it, copilot velocity sits on the same slow foundation — so maybe rewrite first, then copilot. But the window: three competitors shipped copilots in the last two quarters, PMM says we're 12 months behind already, and waiting a year might mean entering dead.

Budget: the board approved £2m for strategic initiatives. Realistically it's £1.2m after the security remediation eats its share, which it will. Deadline: the CEO said the copilot must demo at Camunda Days on 14 May 2027. Though honestly, if the rewrite is the right call the demo date shouldn't drive it — we could show smoke and mirrors. Second thought on revenue: I said 25% attach earlier, but enterprise procurement cycles mean year one is more like 10%, so £700k in year one — the £1.8m is a year-three number. The CPO wants the copilot, the CTO wants the rewrite, they've been at a standoff in every exec meeting since June, and I'm the tiebreak. Which way do we go?

The prototype is expected to increase ARR by up to £1.8m, aligning with strong build–uplift linkage.
Allocating 6 engineers for 8 months against limited budget raises overrun risk by a moderate amount.
Building the copilot without confirmed legal clearance moderately increases compliance block risk.
Starting copilot development reduces the chance of missing the competitive window.
Allocated engineering capacity directly translates into feature velocity.
Diverting large engineering capacity to a big project tends to increase attrition risk.
Legal clearance strongly lowers the risk of enterprise compliance blocking the copilot.
Higher per-seat LLM costs directly reduce net ARR uplift from copilot revenue.
A wider market window reduces the risk of being too late to launch.
A full platform rewrite is expected to improve velocity by reducing architectural drag.
Major rewrites often demoralize teams and increase attrition risk.
Large-scale rewrites often exceed original budget estimates.
Focusing on a slow rewrite can slightly increase the risk of missing the copilot market window.
Increased ARR uplift from the copilot directly contributes to overall ARR growth.
Higher engineering velocity accelerates feature delivery, supporting ARR growth.
Engineering attrition reduces delivery capacity and thus dampens ARR growth.
Budget overruns limit further investment and impair growth prospects.
A legal block on copilot delivery would significantly hinder ARR growth.
Missing the competitive market window reduces potential ARR growth.
